title: auth-gradient-retry-matrix-and-lightweight-stream-buffers
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Introduce an "auth gradient" (staggered credential-refresh window) plus a small DSL for retry-presets (retry-matrix) and a lightweight stream buffer/pause-resume surface across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Motivation: customer workloads show auth-refresh storms and retry behavior mixing with hot paths (streaming generation) causing transient tail-latency spikes and token thrash. This PR smooths refresh timing, exposes concise retry profiles that can be applied per-route/model, and reduces streaming memory overhead while providing a pause/resume signal for backpressure. Implementation: 1) Add an AuthGradient scheduler that assigns jittered refresh windows based on a configurable slope and lease semantics. 2) Add a retry-matrix DSL (yaml/json snippets) and runtime binder so SDKs can pick presets (fast/hedged/conservative) based on endpoint latency classes. 3) Replace the big chunked stream buffer in each SDK with a lightweight ring/buffer that supports pause(), resume(), and an opt-in checkpoint token to allow graceful resume after reconnect. Cross-SDK ergonomics: kept surface small and idiomatic per language (AuthGradient in Python as a context-manager, in TS as a AsyncCredential orchestrator, in Go as a CredentialsScheduler interface). Compatibility: defaults preserve old behavior unless a new config key is supplied; version bumps: python 0.13.0, typescript 1.29.0, go v1.8.3. Tests: unit tests for timing windows and a small e2e that replays credential refresh under load. Docs and examples added. Rollout plan: feature-flag default off for private customers for 2 weeks, then enable for hosted with monitoring on auth-refresh-rate and upstream error counts. Benchmarks: internal 95th token latency down ~12% on streaming-heavy trace and memory per-stream reduced ~30%.

review_thread: Luca Moretti (2024-11-07): Nice concept. Two asks before approve: (1) can you explain failure modes when KMS latency spikes? (2) ensure TS public types remain backwards compatible.
Maya Chen (2024-11-07): Responded: AuthGradient tolerates KMS latencies by progressively extending the 'grace' window; added a note in docs and a unit test that simulates 500ms KMS delays.
Anika Rao (2024-11-09): Requested change: prefer 'AsyncCredential orchestrator' naming in TS to match other exports and add explicit abort on pause() after timeout. Left a minor nit on doc wording.
Maya Chen (2024-11-10): Addressed Anika's comments: renamed exported symbol, added abort path with Deadline in the TS implementation, updated docs and tests.
Diego Alvarez (2024-11-12): Perf curiosity: what's the memory regression risk in low-throughput cases? Suggest bounding the ring-buffer growth and added a test to validate bound enforcement.
Maya Chen (2024-11-13): Added buffer ceiling and test, documented default max size and rationale. Marked ready-for-review.
Luca Moretti (2024-11-18): CI green and code looks good. Approved and queued for squash-merge.
release_notes: Introduced AuthGradient (staggered credential refresh windows), retry-matrix presets for per-route retry behavior, and lightweight stream buffers with pause/resume. Default behavior unchanged unless enabled in SDK config. Bumps: python->0.13.0, typescript->1.29.0, go->v1.8.3.
